title: Liking
hook: People buy from people they like. If they don't like you, your pitch has to do all the work.
statement: People are far easier to persuade when they genuinely like the person asking.
explainer: Even tiny things in common, like a shared hometown, make people more likely to say yes. The fix isn't charm. It's being actually interested in someone before you ask for anything.
sop: Work together visibly when you can.
Skip fake charm. People can tell.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Trust 7, Likability 8, Relevance 6. (7 + 8 + 6) ÷ 3 = 7.0. Higher means people want to say yes to you, not just your offer. Lower means your pitch is carrying everything.
question: Name one prospect you've pitched without really getting to know, and reach out with no ask.
closing_statement: People buy from who they trust, not just what's offered.
caption:
Principle Nº 302: Liking

People buy from people they like. If they don't like you, your pitch has to do all the work.

People are far easier to persuade when they genuinely like the person asking.

Your turn: Name one prospect you've pitched without really getting to know, and reach out with no ask.
